author: reek
body: Drives the REAL simplifier (IR/Simplify.codex, via the `simplify` pass) over real lowered IR. Each function below is one rewrite family the simplifier must apply, written as ordinary Codex so the compiler lowers it to the shape the pass then rewrites -- there is no reimplementation here.

author: reek
body: The battery compiles this file with the DEFAULT pipeline, in which `simplify` does not run, and checks the runtime output against `simplify-check.expected`. That pins the ANSWERS. The proof that the simplifier preserves them is out of band and recorded in `simplify-check.simplify-expected`: the same file compiled with `-Passes simplify` must produce byte-identical serial output and a `SIMPLIFY: rewrites=N` line with N greater than zero. Same answers with the pass on and off is the whole safety claim for a semantics-preserving rewrite; the rewrite count is the proof the pass actually fired rather than passing the program through untouched.
